attributes.probed_form: TWO probes on src/game/game/combat.c, MissileCollideEnemy's inner block only. Baseline banked clean first: 'BASELINE real 8 (insns T86/O86, multiset 0t)', RAW WORDS = 4 of 86, DECODE REGFIELD-ONLY 4. (A) `f32 dz = PF(enemy, offsetof(Enemy, objgrp.coll_pos[2]), f32) - to[2];` split into an uninitialised declaration `f32 dz;` plus the assignment `dz = PF(enemy, offsetof(Enemy, objgrp.coll_pos[2]), f32) - to[2];` placed FIRST among the block's assignments, i.e. exactly where the initialiser used to run -> NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, bytes=935a14727ec6: the split alone is invisible. (B) with (A) in place, the two adjacent assignments TRANSPOSED so the block reads `enemyRadius = radius + PF(enemy, offsetof(Enemy, rad), f32); dz = PF(enemy, offsetof(Enemy, objgrp.coll_pos[2]), f32) - to[2];` -> IMPROVED real 8 -> 0, RAW WORDS 4 -> 0, 'insns exact'. (A) is not decoration: the initialiser has to become a statement before the two can be transposed at all, so (A)+(B) are one lever whose byte-visible half is the ORDER. KEPT: both. The final source diff is five lines in one block and reads as ordinary 2001 C -- five locals declared, then five assignments, `enemyRadius` before `dz` before `dx` before `enemyHeight` before `eh2`.
attributes.residual: NONE. THE MECHANISM, because it generalises and is the reusable half of this record. The residual was four words in one 0x18 window, all REGFIELD-ONLY, all in the VOLATILE FPR scratch: the value loaded from the enemy's coll_pos[2] was f1 in retail and f2 in ours, and the value loaded from the enemy's rad was f3 in retail and f1 in ours, with the two `fsubs`/`fadds` that consume them differing only in those fields. Everything else about the window already agreed -- same opcodes, same load order at 0xa8/0xac/0xb0, same destinations. The two loads are emitted in the order the two ASSIGNMENTS appear in the source, and their scratch numbers are handed out in that same order, so transposing the two source statements transposes the two scratch homes and closes the window. WHY THIS IS WORTH GENERALISING: the block's other four assignments were already in the target's order, so the whole four-word residual came from ONE adjacent pair being written the wrong way round, and nothing in the diff pointed at source order -- it reads as a register-allocation artifact, which is exactly why a rule was authored for it in the first place. The cheap screen for a volatile-FPR recolor of this shape is therefore: list the block's assignments in source order, list the target's load order in the aligned view, and look for a transposed adjacent pair BEFORE reaching for the callee-saved declaration-order laws, which do not govern volatile scratch at all.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: For any candidate: `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py <unit> <fn> --diff --raw` over the differing window. If the two streams' LOAD ORDER differs, this is not the mechanism -- the transposition lever only applies where the schedule already agrees and only the homes differ. If the block has one statement, there is no pair and the screen returns nothing.
hypothesis.count_consequence: Count-neutral by construction: transposing two adjacent assignments that write different locals from independent loads moves register numbers and emission order, never instruction count. Any probe of it that leaves T/O parity has changed something else and is refused on sight -- combat.c is -Cpp_exceptions like most of this image's game TUs, so a count change relocates the TU's extab ranges.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- the aligned raw view was read over MissileCollideEnemy's whole body in both streams before the first probe, and the four differing words plus the byte-identical schedule around them are what suggested the transposition. NOT screened: no census of how many other pins have this shape has been run, so the size of the population is unknown and this hypothesis makes no claim about it.
hypothesis.statement: The same screen should be run against the other volatile-FPR recolor pins before any of them is treated as source-exhausted: the discriminator is a residual confined to consecutive scratch FPRs (f0-f5) in a window whose opcodes and load ORDER already match, in a block containing two or more adjacent assignments whose right-hand sides load independent values. game/sfx/sfx::DmgFxAdd and game/anim/anim::InitAnim were both probed this run and are NOT candidates -- their windows are single expressions with no adjacent assignment pair to transpose, which is recorded in their pin mechanisms -- so the population to screen is the remaining REGISTER_ONLY pins whose differing words decode to FPR fields.
